## How long does the battery last on the WH-1000XM5?

The WH-1000XM5 offers up to 30 hours of battery life with noise canceling on, making them well suited for travel and all-day use. They also feature quick charging that delivers several hours of playback from a short charge.

## Does the WH-1000XM5 have ambient sound or transparency mode?

Yes. The WH-1000XM5 includes Ambient Sound Mode, which lets outside sound in so you can hear your surroundings without removing the headphones. You can toggle it using the NC/AMB button on the left earcup.

## How good is the noise cancellation on the WH-1000XM5?

The WH-1000XM5 uses 2 processors controlling 8 microphones for unprecedented noise cancellation across low, mid, and high frequencies. An Auto NC Optimizer automatically tunes noise canceling based on your wearing conditions and environment, including atmospheric pressure.

## Are the WH-1000XM5 good for phone calls?

Yes. The headphones use four beamforming microphones plus Precise Voice Pickup and advanced signal processing to isolate your voice and reduce background noise for crystal clear hands-free calling.

## How do the WH-1000XM5 charge?

The WH-1000XM5 support quick charging that provides several hours of playback from a short charge. Note that the charging adapter is not included with the WH-1000XM5.

## What colors are available for the WH-1000XM5?

The WH-1000XM5 is available in Silver, Black, Midnight Blue, and Smoky Pink finishes.

## Can the WH-1000XM5 connect to two devices at once?

Yes. The WH-1000XM5 supports Multipoint Connection, letting you connect to two devices simultaneously for seamless switching, such as between a laptop and a phone.

## Does the WH-1000XM5 support high-resolution audio?

Yes. The WH-1000XM5 supports Hi-Res Audio and uses DSEE Extreme processing to upscale compressed audio. They also feature a newly developed 30 mm driver for detailed, awe-inspiring sound quality.

## What is Speak-to-Chat on the WH-1000XM5?

Speak-to-Chat automatically lowers your music and lets in ambient sound when you start talking, so you can hold a conversation without removing the headphones. You can also use Quick Attention by placing your hand over the right earcup for quick conversations.

# Sony’s WH-1000XM5 are cheaper than ever for Black Friday

Last-generation noise-cancelling headphones are still a great option for traveling or staying focused.

Last-generation noise-cancelling headphones are still a great option for traveling or staying focused.

by Brad Bourque

Nov 19, 2026, 7:35 PM UTC

All four colors of the WH-1000XM5 are in stock at the discounted price.

Back in my day, the only “Doorbuster” sales were at physical retail stores. But now, you can get ultra-low prices before Black Friday whether you want to shop in-store or online. One that stands out is the previous-generation Sony WH-1000XM5 noise-canceling headphones, which are marked down to their lowest price ever, just $169.99 at Best Buy. While their MSRP is $399.99, they’ve been spotted as low as $198 in the last few months.

The WH-1000XM5 launched in 2022, and despite having been succeeded by the WH-1000XM6, they’re still an excellent set of headphones. Their active noise cancellation effect is one of the best out there — competitive with the latest models from Bose and Apple — and the sound profile is tighter and more balanced than the older Sony headphones. There are some minor downsides, like a bulky case and all-plastic design, but those seem easier to overlook at this lower price point.

The newer Sony WH-1000XM6 improve the sound and noise cancellation, with quality of life upgrades not present in the XM5, like a folding design and more comfortable headband. However, they’re significantly more expensive, currently discounted to $348 during Black Friday (Amazon, Best Buy), down from their MSRP of $450.

To make shopping a little more confusing, the newer WH-1000XM4C sit between the XM5 and XM6 in terms of price, and are a slightly updated version of the older XM4 model with its foldable design. Our reviewer John Higgins thinks the XM4C’s noise cancellation lags behind, so I’d opt for the XM5 over them, especially at the sale price.
